A Special Area of Conservation covers 182 ha, including some land in private ownership.


== History ==
Since the last Ice Age, Raheenmore Bog has developed in a small basin in the catchment of two major river systems, the
Brosna and the Boyne.  With a depth of 15 meters it forms the deepest raised bog known in Ireland.
The bog was purchased in 1970 by Bord na Móna to mark European Conservation Year.  It was later donated to the National Parks and Wildlife Service. 
It was designated a Ramsar Site in 1988.  Along with Clara Bog, another raised bog in County Offaly, Raheenmore bog has been twinned with Bargerveen,  a Dutch Ramsar Site which required restoration after peat digging was stopped in the 1990s.  Active management has been undertaken at Raheenmore because hydrological investigation showed that the bog was drying out. Peat dams were built to stop water loss.
